title: Food and drink
goal: Order food and drinks at a cha chaan teng or dim sum, and say how it tastes.

notes.p: Between a number (or {{呢|ni1}} this / {{嗰|go2}} that) and a noun, Cantonese needs a measure word that fits the thing. {{個|go3}} is the general one: buns, items you point at. Drinks take {{杯|bui1}} (cup). A bowl is {{碗|wun2}}, a plate {{碟|dip6}}, a portion or order {{份|fan6}}, a bottle {{樽|zeon1}} or {{枝|zi1}}, and people are counted politely with {{位|wai2}}. Before a measure word, two is {{兩|loeng5}}, never {{二|ji6}}.

{{要|jiu3}} + a thing means "I'll have / I want", which is how you order. {{想|soeng2}} means "would like to" and needs a verb after it: {{想飲|soeng2 jam2}} would like to drink, {{想食|soeng2 sik6}} would like to eat. Not wanting something is {{唔要|m4 jiu3}}.

{{有冇…呀？|jau5 mou5 … aa3}} asks "do you have…?". Answer by repeating the verb: {{有|jau5}} yes, or {{冇|mou5}} no. Put {{唔該|m4 goi1}} before or after a request to make it polite. {{啦|laa1}} at the end turns a sentence into a friendly suggestion.
ex: jau5 mou5 dung3 ning2 caa4 aa3
Do you have iced lemon tea?

notes.p: {{好|hou2}} in front of a describing word means "very", and Cantonese uses it even where English just says "I'm hungry". {{好食|hou2 sik6}} is already one word, "tasty", so "really tasty" is {{好好食|hou2 hou2 sik6}}.

{{食|sik6}} eat is low; {{識|sik1}} know is high. {{飲|jam2}} drink rises. {{位|wai2}} rises when you count people, and so does {{魚|jyu2}} fish on its own. Hot {{熱|jit6}} and iced {{凍|dung3}} go in front of the drink.

vocab.note: 食 sik6 (eat) and 識 sik1 (know how to) differ only by tone.
Literally "good to eat". 好飲 (hou2 jam2) = good to drink.
The first 好 = very; 好食 = tasty.
位 (wai2) is the polite word for counting people. Answer 兩位 (two), 三位 (three), and so on.

啦 (laa1) at the end makes a suggestion: "let's".

{{幾多|gei2 do1}} = how many. {{邊度|bin1 dou6}} is where, {{咩|me1}} what, {{點|dim2}} how.

items.en: Do you have BBQ pork buns?
items.why: "Have or not?" is {{有冇|jau5 mou5}}. The "not" of {{有|jau5}} is always {{冇|mou5}}, never {{唔|m4}}.

q: ngo5 jiu3 jat1 bui1 ___ naai5 caa4
items.en: I'll have a hot milk tea.
items.why: Hot is {{熱|jit6}}; {{凍|dung3}} is iced.
{{啦|laa1}} at the end makes a friendly suggestion, "let's". {{呢|ne1}} and {{咩|me1}} would turn it into a question.
You drink coffee: {{飲|jam2}}. {{食|sik6}} is eat; {{識|sik1}} (high tone) is know.
{{要|jiu3}} + a thing is how you order. {{想|soeng2}} needs a verb after it: {{我想飲咖啡|ngo5 soeng2 jam2 gaa3 fe1}}.
{{嗰個|go2 go3}} = that one; {{呢個|ni1 go3}} = this one.
{{唔要|m4 jiu3}} = don't want (a thing). {{想|soeng2}} would need a verb after it.

items.en: What would you like to drink?
items.why: {{咩|me1}} = what. The question word sits where the answer would go: {{你飲茶|nei5 jam2 caa4}}.
A bottle is {{樽|zeon1}}. {{碗|wun2}} would be a bowl.
Before a measure word, two is {{兩|loeng5}}. {{二|ji6}} is only for counting and inside bigger numbers.
Bottles of beer are counted with {{枝|zi1}}.

items.q: Your friends raise their glasses of beer. You say:

roleplay.title: Ordering at a cha chaan teng
roleplay.setup: You and a friend walk into a busy Hong Kong-style café at lunchtime. Get a table, order a drink and something to eat, then ask for the check.
roleplay.persona: You are a busy but friendly waiter at a cha chaan teng in Hong Kong. The menu has milk tea, iced lemon tea, coffee, toast, fried noodles, beef noodles and rice dishes. Ask how many people, then what they want to drink (hot or iced), then what they want to eat. Speak simple colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese using mostly words from levels 1-3, in short sentences. If the learner is stuck, say it again more slowly once, then offer two choices.
opening: fun1 jing4 gwong1 lam4! gei2 do1 wai2 aa3
goals: Say how many people you are
Order a drink with the right measure word

roleplay.title: Dim sum with a friend
roleplay.setup: Your Hong Kong friend Wing has taken you out for dim sum. Decide what to eat, say how the food is, and toast.
roleplay.persona: You are Wing, a relaxed Hong Konger in your thirties, at dim sum with an American friend who is learning Cantonese. Suggest dishes (shrimp dumplings, siu mai, BBQ pork buns), ask what they would like to eat and drink, ask if they are hungry or full, and make a toast. Speak casual colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese using mostly words from levels 1-3, in short sentences, with natural sentence-final particles.
roleplay.opening_en: What would you like to eat?
goals: Say what you'd like to eat
Say whether you're hungry or full
Suggest eating or paying with a let's-sentence
